The brand-new iPhone 18 Pro's variable aperture lens is nearly a full stop wider than the previous generation's fixed aperture: jumping from f/1.78 on the iPhone 17 Pro to f/1.48 (remember: the smaller the number, the larger the aperture).

In theory, this improvement should deliver slightly shallower depth of field, with better separation between the subject and the background — though the difference is relatively subtle. But there are actually four other methods that have been available on the iPhone for years to create a shallow depth of field...

Portrait Mode

The most straightforward way is to use Portrait Mode, which is specifically designed to clearly separate the subject from the background.

It's a purely computational effect (with LiDAR assistance on equipped models), where the system identifies the subject and then artificially blurs everything else. Earlier versions were rather crude, but in recent years it has improved dramatically and performs very well.

Macro Photography

The second method is to use Macro mode, which activates automatically when you get very close to your subject. Once enabled, the iPhone switches to the ultra-wide lens because it can focus at extremely short distances.

In this mode, only a range of a few centimetres remains sharp, with everything beyond gradually blurring out. As you can see in the example below, expect to spend a fair amount of time wiping and cleaning before shooting in this mode! A small yellow flower icon appears in the bottom-right corner of the viewfinder, indicating that the mode is active.

Get Close to Your Subject

You can also use the standard lens — just get very close to your subject to achieve a similar effect. For example:

Before shooting, simply tap on the object or person you want to focus on.

Telephoto Lens

Another factor that affects depth of field is focal length. All else being equal, the longer the focal length, the shallower the depth of field — so using the iPhone's telephoto lens can also create a touch of background blur.

Combining the Three

Using all three methods together yields the best result:

  • Choose the telephoto lens
  • Keep the subject as far from the background as possible
  • Get as close as you can to the subject

This method is ideal for portraits, and on the iPhone 15 Pro and later models, the effect is even more pronounced thanks to the longer focal length.

Summary

The wider variable aperture lens is just one of the many new camera features on the iPhone 18 Pro, and if you use your phone primarily for photography, upgrading is still worth considering. But if your goal is to achieve a background blur effect, there are other methods that can deliver the same result.
